paragraphs: Here's what this chapter shows me, friend. When Ahaz got squeezed, he went looking for help everywhere except the LORD. He paid Assyria out of the LORD's own house, and Chronicles says it "did not help him" (2 Chronicles 28:21). Then he bowed to the gods of Damascus, the very ones who had beaten him. That's asking the team that just whooped you to coach you.

And here's the sting. "In the time of his distress, King Ahaz became even more unfaithful to the LORD" (2 Chronicles 28:22). Distress is a fork in the road. It can push you toward God or it can push you toward anything else with a pulse, and Ahaz took the second road all the way to the end. Chronicles says plainly that those gods "were the downfall of Ahaz and of all Israel" (2 Chronicles 28:23).

But don't close this one thinking it's all dark, because Oded is in there too. One prophet spoke up, some leaders listened, and captives got clothes, sandals, food and drink, and the feeble got a ride on donkeys to Jericho (2 Chronicles 28:9-15). When you're in trouble, run to the LORD first, not last. And when you see someone heading the wrong way, be an Oded, because one honest voice can change what happens next. I'm still baking because the LORD reached into a drawer for me, so I know He's worth running to.
